LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.1: Interactive Speaking
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Interactive Speaking, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we greet one another?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. role play various ways of introducing self in different contexts,

2. watch a video recording of introductions between people and discuss the scenes,

3. work jointly to repeat words on greetings from an audio recording (e.g. assalmu aleikum),

4. listen to Arabic greetings and introductions,

5. dramatise greetings with peers of different gender.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. role play various ways of introducing self in different contexts,
2. watch a video recording of introductions between people and discuss the scenes,
3. work jointly to repeat words on greetings from an audio recording (e.g. assalmu aleikum),
4. listen to Arabic greetings and introductions,
5. dramatise greetings with peers of different gender.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Interactive Speaking together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is developed as the learner builds on their fluency when role playing various ways of

introducing self in different contexts.

• Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits creative ideas and skills when dramatising greetings with

peers of different genders.

2

Values:
Respect: This is enhanced as the learner shows positive regard for self and others when discussing the scenes on introductions

between people.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Gender issues: These are addressed as the learner appreciates differences in greetings to different genders and familiarises

themselves with the acceptable standards.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate this concept about greetings and introduction with similar concepts in English and Kiswahili.
